correctness.rationale: The Hermitian-part unitary reduction gives w=half the Perron root. Continuant expansion gives P_{n,k}=Q_n-(r²-1)Q_{k-1}Q_{n-k-1}. The exact Chebyshev identity makes the adjacent P difference equal to -(r²-1)Q_{n-2k-2}. Perron Rayleigh strictness puts the old root above the unit path edge, where this Chebyshev factor is positive by its known real roots. The successor monic polynomial is negative at the old Perron root and eventually positive, so its Perron root is strictly greater. Covers every integer n>=4, each allowed k, and all real r>1 including crossing the Hermitian spectral edge. Standalone exact polynomial verifier and SPD-root bisection pass; finite checks are not infinity proofs.

originality.rationale: The primary 2013 paper explicitly states the 1<r<2 strict comparison as a conjecture, while proving its counterparts for r<1 and r>=2. The 2014 paper treats two consecutive defects, not this missing single-defect parameter interval. The 2012 cyclic-permutation theorem characterizes global maximizers, which does not logically entail each strict neighboring step. Searches of aliases and related spectral path formulations found no identified full covering theorem, with the general-rearrangement risk transparently recorded.
residual_risks: General spectral edge-rearrangement theorems for symmetric weighted paths might already force the full strict monotonicity; finite web and semantic searches do not prove nonexistence.

value.rationale: Resolves the explicit nontrivial missing interval 1<r<2 in a documented finite-operator numerical-radius conjecture, uniformly for every matrix order and exceptional-link position. Gives a sharp structural location-ordering theorem and a universal simple positive Chebyshev continuant identity spanning both sub- and super-band spectral regimes. This is a mathematically motivated full classification, not a routine numeric estimate or arbitrary example.
